tasks.short: Review conservation grant applications and communicate funding recommendations.

steps.what: Retrieve grant applications, criteria and declared conflicts
Review grant applications for scientific merit and conservation relevance
Compare applications and decide the funding recommendation
Write the grant assessment and funding recommendation record
Submit the final recommendation to the funding body

tasks.design: Configure an indexed review pack and criterion-based assessment form in {DOCS}. Keep appraisal, comparison and recommendation writing human; the scientist sends the final record through {EMAIL}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Reviewers repeatedly locate files and reconstruct the assessment structure.
tasks.enabler_now: Native links and reusable criteria fields remove repeated document preparation.
tasks.still_hard: Merit, uncertainty and competing conservation benefits require accountable judgement.
tasks.human_edge: Explain why one proposal deserves support over another.
tasks.altitude: Make recommendations easier to trace to criteria without automating merit assessment.

reach.learn: Keep evidence and personal judgement distinguishable in the record.

evidence.claim: The digest reports NWO restrictions on generative AI for assessors and European guidance against generative AI in peer review and evaluations.
An indexed pack and native assessment form could reduce clerical preparation; the saving is unmeasured.

assumptions: No generative model receives an application or drafts an assessment. Scheme-specific confidentiality and review rules must still be checked.

The scientist produces application identifier, criterion assessment, reasons, uncertainties and recommendation in s4; retained writing time includes capture. Missing evidence stays explicitly missing.
The form reduces headings and repeated application details, not reasoning. Native views and templates come first.
There is a real submission in s5, but no extra approval gate or saving for the same-system save of the author's record.
unknowns: Whether the funder's existing assessment form already removes this preparation.
research_questions: How much review time is file retrieval and repeated formatting rather than appraisal?

already_counted.description: Write and check the assessment reasons.

incremental.description: Maintain funding criteria and review-pack links.

approvals.approved_version: Exact final assessment, recommendation and funding body recipient; edits or recipient changes require a fresh submission-time check.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: E1 scenario: B=100, R=93, gross=7; upkeep=2 gives central net=5. Existing funder forms may leave no gain.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Design environmental studies, conduct fieldwork and document findings.

steps.what: Define environmental study questions, controls and sampling design
Write the environmental study protocol and field schedule
Conduct field trials or wildlife habitat observations
Record environmental observations, measurements and protocol departures
Calculate the protocol's defined study summaries and comparisons
Interpret study outcomes, uncertainties and limits of inference
Write the study findings and methodological limitations

tasks.design: Use native protocol, data and report templates in {DOCS} and {SPREADSHEET}. A checked workbook calculates predefined summaries; the scientist designs and conducts the study, captures observations and writes the interpretation.
tasks.previous_blocker: Protocols, field records and repeat calculations are rebuilt for each study.
tasks.enabler_now: Reusable field structures and tested workbook formulas can handle the repetitive parts.
tasks.still_hard: Ecological confounding, failed sampling and uncertain habitat effects resist fixed rules.
tasks.human_edge: Choose a defensible study and interpret what the observations establish.

ambition.what: Inspect another predefined comparison within the same defensible study design.

tasks.altitude: Keep scientific ownership while reducing repetitive study administration and calculation.

reach.learn: Record sampling units, dates and protocol departures consistently.

evidence.claim: Native field templates and tested formulas can support study administration and calculations; this environmental-study saving is an E1 scenario.

assumptions: Study design, protocol writing, fieldwork, data capture, calculation, interpretation and findings writing are all inside the task.

The scientist produces sampling unit, site, date, treatment, observed variable, value, unit and departure flags in s4; its retained eight hours include entry and checks. The s2 protocol supplies comparison definitions. Missing or inconsistent inputs stop calculation for manual correction.
Use native forms and formulas before bespoke software. The calculation saving assumes actual repeated manual preparation today, not existing automatic formulas.
No study submission or external notification is implied by this task; the internal record has no author approval gate.
unknowns: Whether repeatable field trials or novel habitat studies dominate the work.
research_questions: Can the workbook reproduce known study summaries while detecting missing sampling units?

already_counted.description: Capture and check observations before calculation.

incremental.description: Maintain templates and test workbook formulas against known results.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: E1 repeatable-study scenario: B=100, R=84, gross=16; upkeep=4 gives central net=12. Range allows substantial variation in field studies.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Prepare, conduct and record conservation fact-finding or mediation sessions.

steps.what: Retrieve documents relevant to the conservation dispute
Prepare the fact-finding agenda and identify contested matters
Conduct fact-finding among government units, landowners and agencies
Mediate options and communicate proposed dispute resolutions
Write the fact-finding and mediation session record
Send the final session record to the agreed participants

tasks.design: Configure a dispute-indexed evidence view and neutral session-record template in {DOCS}. Keep fact-finding and mediation human, then separately write and send the record through {EMAIL}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Evidence retrieval and repeated session-record headings add clerical effort around mediation.
tasks.enabler_now: Native views and templates can preserve case context without interpreting contested statements.
tasks.still_hard: Trust, competing interests and disputed facts require live judgement.
tasks.human_edge: Notice disagreement, preserve neutrality and test whether proposed resolutions are acceptable.
tasks.altitude: Improve traceability around mediation while retaining the relationship work.

reach.learn: Distinguish agreed facts, party claims and unresolved issues.

evidence.claim: Native case views and neutral record templates could reduce retrieval and repeated formatting; the saving is unmeasured.

assumptions: The record is part of the session task, separately priced from listening and mediation; its distribution is a real send.

The scientist produces party identifiers, attributed accounts, agreed facts, disagreements, agreements and actions in s5. Capture and neutrality checks remain in its retained 12 hours; unconfirmed claims are labelled rather than made facts.
Try native case links and templates first. No recording, transcription or automated settlement is assumed.
The scientist's own record has no self-approval gate; the final distribution check belongs to s6.
unknowns: Whether existing mediation records already use a suitable template.
research_questions: Does the template shorten writing while preserving attribution and unresolved disagreements?

already_counted.description: Write and check the neutral session record.

incremental.description: Maintain case links and record headings.

approvals.approved_version: Each exact proposed resolution expressed in the session; new terms are checked before communication.
Exact final session record and distribution list; changes require a fresh send-time check.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: E1 scenario: B=100, R=95, gross=5; upkeep=1 gives central net=4. Most time remains in live sessions.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Develop water conservation or harvest plans from daily ET and site evidence.

steps.what: Gather daily evapotranspiration and weather data for water conservation planning
Capture site constraints, crop needs and plan calculation assumptions
Calculate water balances and defined conservation or harvest scenarios
Compare scenarios and choose suitable water conservation measures
Write the water conservation or harvest plan
Check the plan's assumptions, figures and practical limitations

tasks.design: Configure a daily-data view in {OPS_SYSTEM}, tested water-balance formulas in {SPREADSHEET} and a plan template in {DOCS}. The scientist captures assumptions, chooses measures and writes and checks the plan; no system operates irrigation or sends instructions.
tasks.previous_blocker: Daily data preparation, repeated scenario calculations and plan structure take time.
tasks.enabler_now: Saved data views, reusable formulas and a native plan template can handle repeated preparation.
tasks.still_hard: ET estimates and soil or crop assumptions may not represent the actual site.
tasks.human_edge: Balance water needs, availability and uncertain environmental consequences.

ambition.what: Compare an additional dry-weather scenario before choosing the plan.

tasks.altitude: Move effort from repeated calculations toward defensible conservation choices.

reach.learn: Record the date, location, units and quality of water and crop observations.

evidence.claim: Saved ET views, tested water-balance formulas and native plan templates could reduce repeated preparation; this saving is an E1 scenario.

assumptions: The scientist produces date, location, ET value, ET type, units and source in s1; retained 14 hours include data selection and capture. The scientist produces soil capacity, rooting assumptions, crop coefficients, rainfall, water availability and scenario definitions in s2, with all 15 hours counted.
Missing dates, incompatible units or uncertain coefficients stop s3 for manual resolution during s4. No machine infers a missing measurement.
Use existing native weather or irrigation views and spreadsheet formulas first. Claim calculation savings only where calculations are actually prepared manually today.
Plan writing remains separate from scenario selection. Internal writing and save require no author approval gate; no external send or irrigation action is part of this design.
unknowns: Existing calculation automation and quality of daily ET sources.
research_questions: Can the workbook reproduce a known site's water balance and flag missing dates and unit mismatches?

already_counted.description: Check scenario validity and select practical measures.

incremental.description: Maintain data views and test formulas and templates.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: E1 manual-preparation scenario: B=100, R=68, gross=32; upkeep=7 gives central net=25. Range allows existing automation and source-quality work.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Keep conservation judgement and mediation human while simplifying their records and repeated calculations.
reach: Connect field data, agency communication and documented conservation choices.
skills_to_grow: Design neutral review and session records
role.ambitious_version: A conservation scientist who can show the evidence behind each study, plan and recommendation.
